faq: What does this tool calculate?
The point's global pixel coordinates at a zoom: x from longitude across the world width, y from latitude through the Mercator fraction of the world height.
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map Web Mercator standard — 256-pixel tiles, zoom pyramids, EPSG:3857 geometry in pixel dress.
Can I use this in production GIS?
It is the production formula map libraries use internally — yes for rendering work; measurement belongs to geodesic tools.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84, the frame web maps and GPS share — tile and pixel systems on this page are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — pixels and tiles quantise the world; extra coordinate decimals beyond the cell size are decoration.
Pixel origin?
Top-left: x east from the date line's left edge, y south from the northern cap — screen convention, hence y's southward growth.
Fractional pixels?
Points land between pixels; the calculator reports the fractional truth and renderers round at draw time.
Relation to tiles?
Tile = world pixel ÷ 256 (integer part); in-tile offset = the remainder — two sibling calculators split exactly this division.
Very high zooms?
Zooms into the mid-20s exist in some stacks; the arithmetic is identical, the tiles are mostly imagination and parking lots.
Latitude cap?
±85.0511°, inherited from Mercator — beyond it, no pixel exists.
